Standard: Clearance is provided around the AR subsystem's interface to permit engagement and disengagement procedures with the interface of the targeted tanker/receiver AR subsystem without impacting surrounding structure, FOD generation, or damage to the tanker or receiver. a. Boom Tanker. Boom physical dimensions do not exceed the allowable boom envelope of ATP-3.3.4.5, Maximum Nozzle Envelope figure and Maximum Boom Envelope figure. b. Drogue Tanker. Reception coupling and drogue components do not exceed the allowable envelope defined in ATP-3.3.4.6, Clearance Envelope paragraph, subpart 2, and interior surfaces are free of obstruction. c. Receptacle Receiver. No equipment or structure impinges on area around the receptacle as defined in ATP-3.3.4.5, Clearance Requirements section. All fastener heads around the receptacle are flush with the surrounding structural surface. d. Probe Receiver. Probe installation geometry provides required clearance as defined in ATP-3.3.4.6, Clearance Envelope paragraph, subpart 1. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verify boom design does not exceed allowable envelope in ATP-3.3.4.5, Maximum Nozzle Envelope figure and Maximum Boom Envelope figure. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem verify reception coupling and drogue design meet clearances of ATP-3.3.4.6, Clearance Envelope paragraph, subpart 2, and interior surfaces are free of obstruction. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem show receptacle design and surrounding structure meet clearances of ATP-3.3.4.5, Clearance Requirements section and structural fasteners are installed flush with the surrounding contact area. d. Probe Receiver. Examination of drawings, specifications, and installed subsystem show AR probe installation design meets clearances of ATP-3.3.4.6, Clearance Envelope paragraph, subpart 1. Demonstration.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. 1. Boom nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted receiver receptacle without impacting surrounding structure is demonstrated in laboratory environment. 2. Ground demonstration verifies boom nozzle engagement and disengagement with targeted receptacle-equipped receiver air vehicles without impacting surrounding structure or equipment. b. Drogue Tanker. 1. Probe engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker reception coupling and drogue demonstrates clearances specified in ATP-3.3.4.6, Clearance Envelope paragraph, subpart 2, in a laboratory environment. 2. Ground demonstration with targeted probe-equipped receiver air vehicles show drogue and reception coupling provide clearance to receiver canopy, structure, and equipment. c. Receptacle Receiver. 1. Receptacle system permits targeted tanker boom nozzle engagement and disengagement without impacting or damaging surrounding structure in laboratory environment. 2. Demonstration in a laboratory environment verifies targeted tanker boom nozzle can slide along receptacle slipway without damage or hinderance. 3. Air vehicle ground demonstration verifies engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker boom nozzle without impacting surrounding structure or equipment. d. Probe Receiver. 1. Air vehicle ground demonstration of engagement and disengagement with targeted tanker drogue and reception coupling without interference between probe mast, support structure, probe door, or other air vehicle structure and drogue. 2. Air vehicle ground demonstration shows refueling probe is deployed and stowed (if retractable) without interference and provides clearance to air vehicle canopy and air vehicle structure. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (1) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight testing with receptacle-equipped receivers demonstrates successful engagement and disengagement without impacting surrounding structure or components. Required test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, wet and dry contacts, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight testing verifies hose and drogue can be deployed and stowed without impacting surrounding structure or components. Flight testing with targeted probe-equipped receivers shows engagement and disengagement without impacting surrounding structure or components. Test points include wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight testing with boom-equipped tanker demonstrates successful engagement and disengagement without impact or damage to surrounding structure or components. Test points include worst-case combinations of tanker and receiver gross weights and CGs, at all extents of the boom disconnect envelope, wet and dry contacts, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions, straight and level flight, in turns, and while tobogganing. d. Probe Receiver. Flight testing verifies probe can be deployed and stowed without impacting surrounding structure or components. Flight testing with targeted drogue-equipped tanker demonstrates successful engagement and disengagement without damage to surrounding structure or components. Test points include wet and dry contacts, receiver closure rates of up to 10 ft/s, minimum Mach, maximum Mach, minimum dynamic pressure and maximum dynamic pressure conditions and failure conditions, such as failure to fully extend or deploy.
